Chat generation for agents using Claude via an Anthropic API key.
Chat generation for agents using a personal Claude Max (OAuth) subscription.

Chat generation for agents running your personal Claude Max subscription through the official Claude CLI, inside the hardened llm-runner sidecar. Anthropic does not permit a subscription to be used against its API directly, and the CLI reads its token from the environment rather than from a request header — so this token cannot be kept inside OpenRegister and proxied on your behalf the way an API key is. It is released only to Hermiq, only for you, and only while a turn is running. Personal use only, per Anthropic's terms.

pages.title: Chat
pages._note: Custom page: a streaming chat thread is genuinely custom — SSE token/tool-call consumption with a live assistant bubble, a conversation archive lifecycle driven by Hermiq's payload-marker soft delete, per-message feedback, and an agent-selector empty state are not expressible via the built-in index/detail/dashboard page types (agent-engine-port). Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

config._note: manifest-driven-pages: converted from type:custom — the read path was already createObjectStore agent/hermiq, read-equivalent to the generic objects endpoint (design.md Decision 5). The former Schedule/Last-run derived columns are dropped, not faked — they require a reverse-FK join (Schedule.agentId -> Agent) OpenRegister's calculation engine does not support (design.md Decision 9); the same status is one click away on AgentDetail's run-operations/run-history widgets.

manifest-driven-pages: converted from one opaque type:custom AgentDetail.vue (1570 lines) to a type:detail widget grid (ADR-062: every widget fills its gridHeight exactly, no inner scrollbars, no reserved voids). Six of seven content widgets stay type:custom — Hermiq's AI-governance interactions (dry-run/replay, run-trace observability, tool-catalogue editing, webhook lifecycle) are inherently bespoke, unlike procest/pipelinq's plain-data domain objects (design.md Decision 3). tools is excluded from the data widget and edited only via the Edit-agent header action's existing NcSelect-over-live-catalogue editor (design.md Decision 1). Header actions use config.headerActions: verified at HEAD that CnDetailPage renders config.headerActions via CnActionButtons, while the schema's top-level page.actions[] typed-action array is not yet wired into CnDetailPage's render path — this change follows HEAD over the original REQ-008 wording (flagged for the reviewer). AgentFormModal/AgentVersionHistoryDialog/AgentFactsheetDialog self-resolve the current agent id (and, for version history, the owner-only rollback gate) from the route when opened via open-modal, since open-modal action props are static JSON, not resolved against @objectId at HEAD.

widgets.title: Run KPIs
widgets._note: Agent-scoped run totals from the computed /api/analytics endpoint (success rate, latency, tokens) — not an OR object-count query, so stats-block cannot bind it (ADR-049). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-kpis -> agent-kpis.

widgets.title: Skills
widgets._note: skillInstalls attach/detach against the tenant Skill catalogue — the reverse of an object-list FK-child-collection shape (design.md Decision 3). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-skills -> agent-skills.

widgets.title: Tool governance
widgets._note: Combines the schema-scoped tool-grant editor and the EU AI Act art.12/14 tool-invocation audit table — two read/write surfaces over the SAME ADR-063 derived catalogue capability (design.md Decision 3). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-tool-governance -> agent-tool-governance.

widgets.title: Run operations
widgets._note: Schedule attach/edit, Dry run, Run now, cost estimate, budget status and the webhook trigger all read/write the SAME schedule object and share previewResult/runError state — the manifest grid has no cross-widget state channel, so they stay one widget (design.md Decision 3). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-run-operations -> agent-run-operations.

widgets.title: Memory
widgets._note: Wraps the existing AgentMemoryPanel.vue unchanged (char-budget bar, consolidation nudge, entries) — a bespoke surface over a non-OR-collection endpoint (design.md Decision 3, task 2). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-memory -> agent-memory.

widgets.title: Run history
widgets._note: Per-row trace expand-and-cache, a dead_letter-only Re-run, and a Replay dry-run + diff preview — object-list's static columns/rowRoute shape has no per-row expand or conditional actions (design.md Decision 2/3). Resolved via page.slots.widget-agent-run-history -> agent-run-history.

pages.title: Approvals
pages._note: Custom page: the reviewer inbox is reviewer-scoped (not owner-scoped OR objects) with guarded approve/deny actions and the org kill-switch — not expressible via the built-in index page type. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Memory
pages._note: Custom page: agent memory combines the createObjectStore agent collection (picker) with tenant-scoped Memory/Session objects, a char-budget bar, the consolidation nudge + manual consolidate, and OR-search recall — not expressible via the built-in index/detail page types. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Sessions
pages._note: Custom page: conversation sessions are the OpenRegister agents resource (picker) plus tenant-scoped Session/SessionTurn objects served agent-scoped (/agents/{id}/sessions, /recall), not the generic objects/{register}/{schema} path, so the built-in index page type cannot express it. Split from Memory so chats are their own surface.

config._note: Converted from type:custom to the default index layout. The agentskills.io import/export + install-onto-agent actions are NOT dropped — they move to the skill-row-actions widget behind their existing guarded endpoints (same pattern as agent-template-row-actions). skill-maturity adds the maturityLevel dots column (consumer cell widget 'maturity-dots', App.vue cellWidgets) and the rowRoute onto the SkillDetail scorecard page.

skill-maturity (mirrors EvalDatasetDetail): the durable maturity scorecard home — per-level pass/fail + reasons + evidence timestamps, the owner-guarded Qualify action and the action-gated Attest-L4 form live in the one custom skill-maturity-scorecard widget; qualify/attest are bespoke SkillMaturityController endpoints, not OR object CRUD.

widgets.title: Maturity scorecard
widgets._note: Per-level L1–L7 scorecard + Qualify + Attest-L4. Resolved via page.slots.widget-skill-maturity-scorecard -> skill-maturity-scorecard.

config._note: hermiq-github-store: the retired AgentTemplateGallery page, renamed 'Store' and repointed from /agent-templates to /store — the underlying local list is UNCHANGED (register:hermiq schema:agenttemplate, same agent-template-row-actions row actions), so agent-template browse/approve/export/instantiate/publish-to-GitHub behaviour is regression-safe. What changes is the below-header agent-template-github-store widget: it now discovers BOTH agent templates AND skills (per-kind filter) — an installed skill is not an agenttemplate row, so it does not appear in THIS table; it surfaces on the separate /skills page instead (design.md Decision 4 — /skills stays separate). Originally converted from type:custom — AgentTemplateController::list() is a bare findAll(['limit'=>200]) with no extra scoping beyond OpenRegister's own RBAC, read-equivalent to the generic objects endpoint (design.md Decision 5). Write actions (Use this template / Approve / Export) stay behind their existing guarded endpoints via the agent-template-row-actions widget — Approve is NEVER a declarative object-op, since it gates through ActionAuthService::requireAction('agenttemplate.approve-quarantined') server-side, a check the generic OR object-patch path does not express (design.md Decision 6).

pages.title: Dashboard
pages._note: Single dashboard (/analytics merged in and dropped). Custom widgets MUST be declared as config.widgets type:'custom' + config.layout + a TOP-LEVEL slots map ('widget-<id>' -> registry key) — the decidesk pattern. A top-level widgets[] instead makes CnPageRenderer mount a bare CnWidgetGrid and skip CnDashboardPage, so no page header renders and nothing carries the 56px nav-toggle clearance.

pages.title: Tenant ops
pages._note: Custom page: per-org quota usage + EU AI Act audit export (download) over OpenRegister objects/AuditTrail, capability-gated to org owners/admins — not expressible via the built-in index/dashboard page types. Standard nav page.

config._note: manifest-driven-pages: converted from type:custom (design.md Decision 8) — the outer list is a flat type:index (name/description only; no per-row run controls) since the old nested card-with-embedded-runs-and-picker shape does not fit a one-row-per-object index. Per-dataset run management moves to the new EvalDatasetDetail page's eval-run-panel widget.

manifest-driven-pages (design.md Decision 8): hosts the per-dataset agent-picker + Run + run history as one custom eval-run-panel widget — 'Run' has no OR-object equivalent (the one bespoke src/api/evals.js action; every other eval path is object CRUD).

widgets.title: Run
widgets._note: Agent-picker + Run + this dataset's run history. Resolved via page.slots.widget-eval-run-panel -> eval-run-panel.

pages._note: Settings-section page: a per-organisation policy FORM (GuardrailPolicy has no name/title property — inputFilters/outputFilters/toolPolicy/enabled only), so the built-in index page type has no meaningful columns to list. Reached from the nav settings foldout (section:settings).
pages.title: Guardrail policy

config._note: Settings-section page: high-risk AI features eligible for Dutch Algoritmeregister publication. Read path is a plain findAll over agentaifeature, so the built-in index type is read-equivalent.
Settings-section page: compliance controls per framework. EU AI Act audit export / retention / incidents are folded in here (moved off tenant-ops).

pages._note: Custom page rendering the standard nc-vue list UI (CnDataTable): MCP tools are resolved live from OpenRegister's tool registry, NOT a hermiq schema, so type:index (which requires register+schema) cannot express it.
pages.title: MCP tools

config._note: Agent graphs are plain OpenRegister objects, so the browse/search surface is a standard type:index — no bespoke list code. Authoring happens on GraphDetail, which is type:custom because a direct-manipulation canvas is not expressible as a widget grid.

pages.title: Graph
pages._note: Custom page: a direct-manipulation canvas over an agentflow node/edge document (drag to place, drag-to-connect, per-node config, run + trace). No built-in page type expresses graph authoring — index/detail/dashboard are all record-shaped. Controls live in the NcAppSidebar so the canvas gets the full width.

steps.title: Welcome to Hermiq
steps.body: Hermiq runs autonomous agents against a local LLM. Point it at your Ollama host and test the connection once — agents can't run without a reachable model.

steps.title: Test connection
steps.body: Probe the endpoint and confirm Hermiq can reach your models. The first model discovered becomes the default.

steps.title: Welcome to Hermiq
steps.body: Let's take a quick tour. Hermiq lets you build autonomous AI agents, give them skills and tools, and run them on a schedule.
Agents are the heart of Hermiq. Open Agents to see them and define your own.

steps.title: Your agent catalog
steps.body: This is where your agents live. Use New to create one — give it a prompt, pick a model, and add optional tools and skills.
Skills give agents new abilities. Browse the Skills catalog to see what you can add.
MCP tools, Compliance, Guardrail policy, and the Algorithm register all live in Settings now. Open Settings to explore them.

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: That's the tour. Open Settings any time to re-run this walkthrough or the setup wizard.
